# /wall/[id]/prompt-packs

Step 1 of the pack picker: write a custom prompt for this wall, or browse
the curated pack catalog and open one. It is a creator-only screen inside
F7, reached only from the wall's own prompt-pack entry point.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Route | `/wall/[id]/prompt-packs` |
| Router file | `app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/index.tsx` |
| Flows | F7 Wall creation and administration |
| Position in flow | step 1 of 2, `/family` -> here -> `/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/[packId]` |
| Data calls | one read (`listPromptPacks`), one write (`injectCustomWallPrompt`) |
| Shared surface | `ScreenHeader` |

Cited to hs2studio/scribl-app at `c1b3c2d` on `main`, clean tree.

## Features

| Feature | Where it lives |
|---------|----------------|
| Write and submit a custom prompt for this wall, up to `MAX_CUSTOM_PROMPT_LENGTH` characters | `app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/index.tsx:36-45`, `82-92` |
| Browse the pack catalog with each pack's title and prompt count | `app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/index.tsx:113-131` |
| Open a pack to choose prompts from it | `app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/index.tsx:118-123`, pushes to the sibling `[packId]` screen |
| Retry the pack list on load failure | `app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/index.tsx:57-65` |

The custom-prompt card is deliberately first in the list, ahead of the
packs, per the screen's own comment quoting the client: "at the top, we
should have then create your own prompt, and then pick from the prompt
packs" (`app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/index.tsx:31-35`). The same comment
explains why the custom prompt is inline here rather than its own route: a
`/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/custom` path would collide with the sibling
`[packId]` dynamic segment and render as an unknown pack.

This screen is reachable only from a creator-gated entry point on `/family`
(`app/family.tsx:1092`); the screen itself carries no gate of its own, and
its own doc comment calls that entry point "a courtesy, not the boundary"
since the server enforces creator-only on the write regardless
(`app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/index.tsx:14-19`).

## Data calls

Both the custom prompt and pack selection are real writes, not read-only
browsing. Choosing a pack on the next screen persists to the wall; the
catalog view itself only reads the list and writes the custom prompt.

| Client method | Endpoint | Handler |
|---------------|----------|---------|
| `listPromptPacks()` | `GET /prompt-packs` | `backend/lambda/handlers/prompt-packs-list.ts` |
| `injectCustomWallPrompt(channelId, text)` | `POST /walls/:channelId/prompts` | `backend/lambda/handlers/wall-prompts-create.ts` |

Both methods are on `src/data/http.ts` (`listPromptPacks:411-414`,
`injectCustomWallPrompt:433-447`). The screen calls the pack list through
`usePromptPacksStore.load()` (`app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/index.tsx:23`,
`27-29`) and the custom-prompt write through
`useWallPromptsStore.injectCustom()` (`:24`, `36-45`), not directly off
`dataClient`.

## State in, state out

**Reads on entry.** The route's `id` param as `channelId`
(`app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/index.tsx:22`); the pack catalog, loaded on
mount (`:27-29`).

**Writes on mount.** None beyond the catalog fetch.

**Writes on exit.** On a successful custom-prompt submit: a new prompt row
on the server for this wall, then a bounce back to `/family` with the wall
in context (`:41-43`). Opening a pack instead writes nothing here; the write
happens on the next screen.

## Notes for planning

Authored here, not read out of the app.

### The gate is a courtesy, and the code says so

Most creator-only screens in this app enforce nothing client-side and rely
entirely on the server. This one is explicit about it in its own comment
(`:14-19`): the entry point on `/family` is the UX gate, the 403 on write is
the real one. Worth calling out as the pattern to replicate anywhere else a
creator-only action needs a client affordance.

### Custom prompt authoring is a workaround for the router, not a design choice

The custom-prompt card sits inline on the catalog screen because a sibling
route would collide with `[packId]` (`:31-35`). That is a router constraint
dressed up as a placement decision. If prompt authoring grows beyond one
text field, it will need a real route, and the workaround will not scale
with it.
